title: the Rajasuya
hook: Bhima and Jarasandha wrestle for days and nights; the captive kings walk free, and Jarasandha's son is put on his father's throne
carry: leave the other side something real

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Rajasuya's road ran through Jarasandha's hall at midnight, where three guests refused his welcome — they gave their names, and their reason. Did you say a reason plainly? Day seven hundred fifty-five.

Jarasandha does one thing first. He has his son, Sahadeva, installed as king. Whatever happens next, Magadha won't be left without a ruler. A king who holds other kings in chains still makes sure his own people will have someone on the throne. Then he takes off his crown, binds his hair, and steps out to meet Bhima. No armies. No weapons. Two men, bare-handed, and a crowd of citizens gathering to watch. The prison doors hang on how it ends.
screen: `HIS SON MADE KING FIRST.` → `NO ARMIES, NO WEAPONS.` → `BHIMA AND JARASANDHA.`

segments.voice: They wrestle, the text says, without stopping for food or rest, day and night, for days on end. They grip and throw. They strike with arms and knees. And then, at last, Jarasandha grows tired, and pauses. Krishna sees it, and speaks a word to Bhima, and Bhima takes it as his signal. He lifts Jarasandha high, whirls him around, and brings him down, and the king of Magadha dies. Here's where the story could turn into a conquest. It doesn't. The three go straight to the prison and open it. The captive kings walk out. And they turn to Krishna and ask, what can we do for you? Krishna's answer is small, almost polite. Yudhishthira wants to perform the Rajasuya, he says. Help him. That's all. Then something smaller happens. Jarasandha's son, Sahadeva, comes out with his ministers, bowing low, offering gifts. The kingdom is theirs for the taking. Krishna gives it back. He reassures the young man, and installs him as king of Magadha, on his father's throne. Remember where Krishna's counsel pointed at Indraprastha: before anyone could be honored, the kings in that prison had to go free. Now look at the order of what he actually did. Free the prisoners first. Ask them for nothing but help with a rite. And leave the defeated king's family their home. The Rajasuya is still to come. But here is one picture of what the rite is for, in Krishna's hands.
screen: `DAY AND NIGHT, BARE-HANDED.` · `JARASANDHA TIRES, AND FALLS.` · `THE PRISON OPENS.` · `THE SON GETS THE THRONE.` · then, large: `FREE THEM FIRST. GIVE THE THRONE BACK.`

segments.voice: Let the breath settle. Recall a time you came out ahead of someone: an argument, a contest, a deal. Picture what you did next. Was there something you could have left them, or given back? There's no need to grade yourself. Just notice where the moment after winning sits in you. If you pray, you can hold that other person in mind for a few breaths. If you don't, simply wish them well. The bell holds the time.
The Rajasuya. Today, its road opens a prison, and asks the freed kings only for their help, and hands a fallen king's throne to his son.
Your line: leave the other side something real. Today, when you win something, leave the other side something real. Day seven hundred fifty-five.

howItsDone: In traditional Indian wrestling, kushti, wrestlers train in an akhara, and Hanuman and Bhima are honored there as patrons of strength.

fork.setup: you're Krishna. Jarasandha is dead, and his son bows before you with gifts. Magadha is yours for the taking. what do you do?

leave the kingdom with no king.
fork.reveal: he reassures the young Sahadeva and installs him as king of Magadha. the prisoners are freed; the defeated family keeps its home.

original.note: Sanskrit bhīmasena: Bhima's fuller name, the Pandava who wrestles Jarasandha.

trapdoor: what you thought: a wrestling match to win a kingdom.
what it means: a fight to free captive kings, after which the kingdom goes back to the fallen king's son.
what a scholar hears: Krishna asks the freed kings only to help the Rajasuya, so the rite's support begins as gratitude.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Sabha Parva, Jarasandha-vadha Parva (Sahadeva installed; the wrestling; Jarasandha's death; the kings freed; Sahadeva made king of Magadha)

notes: All paraphrase. The text gives a specific span of days for the fight; it was left out on purpose. Confirm 'day and night, without food or rest'.
Confirm that Jarasandha installed his son Sahadeva before the fight, and that he removed his crown and bound his hair.
Manner of death: written as lifted, whirled and brought down. Popular retellings have Bhima tearing him in two; confirm Ganguli's wording and adjust if needed.
Confirm Krishna prompts Bhima when Jarasandha tires; the line is paraphrased loosely ('now').
Confirm the freed kings ask what they can do, Krishna asks only that they help Yudhishthira's Rajasuya, and Krishna installs Sahadeva.
Confirm that citizens gathered to watch the fight.
howItsDone: confirm the kushti/akhara description and that Hanuman and Bhima are honored as patrons there.
